source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"One pad upper right chest, one lower left, or anterior-posterior per protocol, rather than any placement being acceptable as the newer team member is currently assuming","B":"Pad placement having fairly little bearing on defibrillation effectiveness for this client, similar to what the newer team member is currently assuming","C":"Placing pads directly over clothing without direct skin contact, which is not the correct technique for this particular resuscitation procedure","D":"Placing both pads on the same side of the chest, which is not the correct placement for this particular procedure"}}
source_row.rationale: Standard defibrillator pad placement typically involves placing one pad on the upper right chest (below the clavicle, to the right of the sternum) and the other pad on the lower left side of the chest at the cardiac apex (anterolateral placement), or using an anterior-posterior placement in certain situations, per device instructions and protocol, ensuring direct skin contact (not over clothing) for effective current delivery.
source_row.source_name: American Heart Association — ACLS Defibrillation Guidelines
source_row.stem: A nurse is assisting with defibrillation during a cardiac arrest, and a newer team member assumes pad placement doesn't really matter as long as both pads are somewhere on the chest. Correct pad placement generally instead involves:
